messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Su <peter.su@medisys-inc.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cust. Key: operator-access playbook + subprocessor geo-fencing (DPA addendum request)

Hi Peter —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To keep the procurement track moving, Medisys asked we produce a short DPA addendum that:

- Narrows operator access windows for private deployments (VPC / on-prem)
- Lists subprocessors and geofence commitments for EU-resident data
- Confirms evidence we can provide showing operator actions (audit logs, session recordings, KMS access records)

Quick ask: can you confirm the two items below so we can draft the addendum and get it over to your legal team?

1) Target operator maintenance window: are you comfortable with a 2-hour weekly maintenance window plus emergency breakglass approvals (we'll include explicit approval flow)?
2) Subprocessor gating: do you require that any operator-side subprocessors who might process metadata be limited to EU-only locations, or is an EU + EEA list acceptable?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the questions your security team requested (Medisys_DPA_questions.xlsx).

We'll draft a proposed addendum that includes: strict operator SLA for access windows, mandatory audit evidence retention (90 days initially, extendable), and a subprocessor manifest with geo-fencing commitments.

Irene and Karthik — looping you in for proposed wording and the operational evidence we can commit to provide.

Next steps: I'll draft a one-page addendum and a mutual action plan (MAP) once Peter confirms the two bullets above.

Thanks,

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Cc: Medisys Legal <legal@medisys-inc.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 13:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cust. Key: operator-access playbook + subprocessor geo-fencing (DPA addendum request)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Quick answers from our side:

- Maintenance window: 2-hour weekly window is acceptable for routine maintenance. For emergency access, we'll need documented approval from our security reviewer (security@medisys-inc.com) and that access to be limited to named operator roles only.
- Subprocessors: we prefer EU-only for any subprocessors who see metadata. If that's a non-starter, list the subprocessors and jurisdictions and we can escalate.

Medisys Legal is CC'd and will review your proposed addendum. We typically want audit evidence for any operator action for at least 180 days (can be negotiated).

I'll review the spreadsheet and push any high-priority questions to legal.

Regards,
Peter
Peter Su
Head of Cloud Ops | Medisys Inc
peter.su@medisys-inc.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cust. Key: operator-access playbook + subprocessor geo-fencing (DPA addendum request)

Marissa / Irene —

I drafted the operational language we should include in the addendum. High-level points:

- Operator access model:
  * Maintenance window: 2-hour weekly window, pre-scheduled with Medisys technical contact.
  * Emergency breakglass: access requires escalation via an on-call POA + email confirmation to security@medisys-inc.com with an after-action report within 24 hours.
  * Named roles only: engineer/resource access assigned to explicit operator user IDs; no generic accounts.

- Evidence commitments:
  * Audit logs (KMS envelope unwrap events, session start/stop, commands executed) retained for 180 days by default; can be extended to 365 days for regulated workloads.
  * Session recordings for operator console sessions kept for 90 days and made available on security request within 48 hours.
  * Hash-only telemetry: request/response payloads are never stored in plaintext in our control plane; we can produce hash traces for provenance checks.

- Subprocessor gating:
  * We can commit that any subprocessors with potential access to metadata will be EU-resident for this engagement. Non-EU subprocessors (where present) will be avoided or blocked by contract.

I have upload perms to the shared MAP folder here: https://redwood-inference.app/drive/Shared/MD-2027-0142/DPA-evidence — I'll drop a draft addendum and a short MAP (one page) by EOD.

If you want, I can include exact log fields we will provide (timestamps, user id, operation, KMS key id, resource id).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference

From: Medisys Legal <legal@medisys-inc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Peter Su <peter.su@medisys-inc.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cust. Key: operator-access playbook + subprocessor geo-fencing (DPA addendum request)

Marissa / Team —

Attached is a redline of the DPA addendum we discussed (DPA_Addendum_Redline.docx). A few practical notes from Legal:

1) We need explicit definitions for the terms ‘operator’ and ‘subprocessor’ in the addendum; please ensure operator is scoped to named roles and does not include third-party contractors unless explicitly listed.
2) Jurisdiction guarantee: Medisys requires a contractual guarantee that subprocessors processing metadata will be EU-resident for the life of the contract. Please confirm whether Redwood will accept a negative covenant (no non-EU subprocessors) or provide a periodic evidence/attestation.
3) Audit evidence delivery: Medisys needs a guaranteed SLA for producing evidence (90 days for most logs; 30 days for emergency requests). Please flag any operational constraints.

We redlined a clause around indemnity tied to unauthorized operator access; we can negotiate but need to see the proposed final wording.

Please advise whether the redline aligns with the operational commitments Karthik outlined; if yes, our legal team can circulate an executable PDF for signature.

Kind regards,
Medisys Legal
legal@medisys-inc.com

Attachment: DPA_Addendum_Redline.docx (redline of proposed addendum)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Su <peter.su@medisys-inc.com>, Medisys Legal <legal@medisys-inc.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cust. Key: operator-access playbook + subprocessor geo-fencing (DPA addendum request)

Team —

Thanks for the redline and the clarifications. Summary and proposed MAP so we're all aligned:

1) Operational commitments (Redwood):
   - Weekly maintenance window: 2 hours, pre-scheduled.
   - Emergency breakglass: documented escalation, named operator roles only, after-action report within 24 hours.
   - Audit evidence: KMS unwrap events, session start/stop, user IDs, command logs retained 180 days; session recordings 90 days.
   - Subprocessors: EU-only for metadata-processing subprocessors; negative covenant in addendum.

2) Legal asks (Medisys):
   - Definitions: explicit operator/subprocessor language (we accepted the examples in your redline).
   - Evidence SLA: Redwood to produce requested evidence within 48 hours for emergency requests; 7 business days for standard requests.
   - Indemnity: flag for negotiation — we will present limited language that ties to proven operator negligence.

3) Next steps / timeline (MAP):
   - Redwood to push final addendum reflecting the negative covenant and evidence SLA into the shared folder by EOD Tue (link below).
   - Medisys Legal to review redline and prepare executable PDF for signature (target Wed).
   - DocuSign link will be shared here when ready: https://docusign.com/summary/MD-2027-0142/dpa-addendum

I attached the final PDF we'll try to circulate (dpa-addendum-final.pdf). Please confirm if the evidence SLA above is acceptable; if so, we'll route to DocuSign and mark the procurement milestone as "DPA addendum signed".

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call if teams want to walk the addendum live.

—Marissa
